note: Dei Filius ch. 3 para. 1 states that God revealing 'nec falli nec fallere potest'. The premise splits this into two consequences of the classical attributes: God asserts only what he believes (cannot deceive) and believes only what he holds as known (cannot be deceived). The council asserts the two inabilities of God as revealer; it does not derive them from intellect and will or phrase them as conditions on asserting and believing.
